_comment: Ad density and behaviour, read at runtime by public/ads.js. This file is the committed default; server/index.js serves GET /ads-config.json and merges the ADS_CONFIG environment variable over the top, so densities can be retuned by setting one Fly secret without rebuilding or redeploying the app. See docs/action-plan.md for the tuning procedure and docs/revenue-model.md for what each setting is worth.
_maxSlotsPerPage: Hard ceiling on how many slots fill on one page, counted in document order; the rest are dropped. 0 disables ads without touching markup. The markup sets the intended density (three on content pages); this is the ceiling and the live tuning lever. Set it below the number of slots in the HTML to thin every page at once.
_types: Per-format kill switch. A disabled format never loads and its slot collapses. Use this to pull one unit that is underperforming without editing 282 pages.
_socialBar: Adsterra's dismissible floating Social Bar. It waits for time on page, and on editorial pages also for meaningful scrolling. It is allowed on the app surfaces now, but never while a call or chat is live and never during matchmaking - ads.js re-checks that at load time - so a remotely controlled creative can never cover the call controls mid-conversation.
_searchAnchor: A controlled 320x50 adhesive shown only while the voice matcher is actively searching. It disappears before connecting and stays absent for the full call. The visitor can dismiss it for 24 hours.
_pauseDuringCall: While a voice call or text chat is live, no slot starts loading, retries a host, or collapses. Ads already on screen stay exactly as they are. This is what keeps a long call free of movement while still earning from impressions placed before it started. Searching for a match is deliberately NOT counted as live: the screen is static and the user is waiting, so that is when the call screen's slots fill.
_callScreenCap: Frequency cap for the slots inside the call screen (#callPanel): they serve a network ad on at most one call in every everyNCalls, counted per browser tab session. On the other calls the reserved space gets one of our own promos (see fallback) or collapses. 1 means no cap. Separately and always on: a slot still loading when a match connects is abandoned invisibly inside its reserved space, so no ad ever appears at the connect moment.
_lazyRootMargin: How far ahead of the viewport a slot begins loading. Larger fills sooner and wastes more impressions on users who never scroll that far; smaller risks an empty slot when the user arrives.
_fillTimeoutMs: How long one serving host is given to put something in the frame before the next host is tried, while the slot is still off screen. Generous on purpose: nobody is looking at it, and a short deadline throws away real fills on slow mobile connections.
_visibleFillTimeoutMs: The same deadline while the slot IS on screen. Much shorter, because every extra second is a second of blank space someone is staring at. An ad blocker or a filtering resolver means the slot will never fill, and this is how fast the page takes that space back.
_fallback: What to put in a slot when the ad network never fills it - most often because the visitor runs an ad blocker or a filtering DNS resolver, which is a large share of this audience. Rather than collapsing to nothing, the slot shows one of our own promos. These are plain first-party HTML with no external request of any kind, so nothing exists for a blocker to block. Never labelled Sponsored, because they are our own content and calling them sponsored would be a lie. Set enabled:false to go back to collapsing.

promos.body: What we protect, what we cannot, and the controls worth knowing.

_backfill: The demand waterfall for a slot Adsterra could not fill. An unsold Adsterra impression earns nothing and the house promo that currently takes that space earns nothing either, so each network below is offered the slot in turn and the promo only takes what they all decline. Order matters: put the highest paying network first, the rest see only what it declined. This never runs on a slot Adsterra did sell, so no slot carries two competing tags. TO ENABLE: set enabled:true, fill in each network's src and zones from its dashboard, and add every src origin to the ADS_SCRIPT_HOSTS environment variable (e.g. fly secrets set ADS_SCRIPT_HOSTS='https://a.com https://b.com') - a host missing from script-src is dropped silently by the browser and looks exactly like an unsold slot. render is 'script' for a tag that writes beside itself (Monetag, PropellerAds MultiTag) or 'iframe' for a document.write tag needing its own frame (HilltopAds, classic direct tags). zones maps a slot size - or 'native' - to that network's zone ID; a network with no zone for a size is skipped rather than loaded empty, so a partially filled map is safe and a network can run for one format only.
_minViewportHeight: Below this viewport height, in-app slots inside the call and chat UI are skipped entirely, so a short phone screen is not mostly advertisement.
